concept.name: Uptrend
concept.definition: A trend characterized by a series of ascending peaks and troughs — successively higher highs and higher lows. It is the classical chart-based description of sustained demand exceeding supply; an analytical construct, not evidence that prices must keep rising.
concept.intuition: Each rally carries price further than the last, and each dip stops at a higher floor — a staircase climbing upward.
concept.mechanics: Identified when each successive swing high exceeds the prior swing high and each successive swing low holds above the prior swing low. Often visualized with an up trendline connecting two or more rising lows; the uptrend is conventionally considered intact while price stays above that line or the last higher low.
concept.failure_modes: The structure breaks the moment a lower low prints, but that break is only confirmable after it happens; sharp news-driven declines can invalidate an uptrend without warning.
concept.misconceptions: That every dip in an uptrend is a buying opportunity; any pullback can deepen into a full reversal, and the difference is clear only in retrospect.
concept.example: A stock rises 50 to 55, pulls back to 52, rises to 58, then pulls back to 54: higher highs (55, 58) and higher lows (52, 54) mark an uptrend.
